Zodiac

Alphonse Mucha, 1896

Colour lithograph

Art Nouveau poster: flowing hair and ornament in peach, terracotta and gold.

Use this style

Alphonse Mucha, Zodiac, 1896. Colour lithograph. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Mucha designed Zodiac in 1896 as a calendar for the Paris printer F. Champenois, and the magazine La Plume also issued it. A woman in profile wears an elaborate jewelled headdress, framed by a halo carrying the signs of the zodiac. It was printed as a colour lithograph, one stone per colour.

This is Art Nouveau at its most typical: flowing hair, a firm outline around every shape, flat areas of soft colour and dense ornament around the edges. Mucha's posters for Sarah Bernhardt had made him famous in Paris, and the look became so tied to him that people called it the Mucha style.

How it looks on your photo

A warm style. Photos turn peach, terracotta and soft gold, with a light texture and slightly firmer edges. It flatters portraits and suits warm scenes. Cool colours such as sky blue are replaced by warm ones.
